questions.title: Read an Unconditional Probability from a Setup - pick the plain rate for the first event out of a setup that also states a second rate and a conditional rate
Read the Second Unconditional Probability from a Setup - pick the plain rate for the second event out of a setup whose conditional rate is about that same event
Identify a Conditional Probability from Its Wording - pick out the rate that is restricted to one group, rather than the unconditional rate about the same event
Interpret a Conditional Event in Words - translate the notation B|A back into a sentence, against distractors that reverse the condition or swap it for AND or OR
Multiplication Rule for a Joint Probability - compute P(A AND B) from an unconditional rate and the conditional rate given in the same setup
Interpret a Joint Event in Words - translate A AND B into a sentence, against distractors that turn it into a conditional or into the inclusive OR
Test Two Events for Independence - compute the product of the two unconditional probabilities, compare it with the joint probability, and state the conclusion
Addition Rule for a Union Probability - compute P(A OR B) by subtracting the overlap, and recognise why adding the two rates alone overcounts
Interpret a Union Event in Words - translate A OR B into a sentence, targeting the assumption that OR in probability is exclusive
Test Two Events for Mutual Exclusivity - compute the joint probability, compare it against zero, and distinguish the mutually-exclusive test from the independence test

Full Workup of a Survey with Two Conditionals - sort four survey figures into two unconditional and two conditional probabilities, interpret each conditional in words, then apply the multiplication and addition rules and test for mutual exclusivity

Poll Proportions, a Complement, and a Headcount - read a sample size and three yearly approval rates off a poll summary, take the complement of one rate, and convert another rate back into a whole number of respondents

Roulette Single Spin - Sample Space, Simple Events, Complements and Independence - count pockets to find three probabilities on one spin, then decide whether odd is the complement of even, name a mutually exclusive pair, and test a colour-or-range pairing for independence
Probability of Seven Roulette Bets - count the pockets each bet covers and divide by 38, across seven bets of different sizes
